title: No Post-Credits Scene in New Resident Evil Movie—Here's Why
summary:
You know the drill: the movie ends, the credits roll, and you sit there waiting for a secret scene. Well, for the new Resident Evil movie, you can head straight to the lobby. There is no post-credits scene at all. Director Zach Cregger says everything he wanted to say happens before the credits.

This is a big deal because post-credits scenes have become super common in franchise movies. And Resident Evil has nine main video games, so there's plenty of story to tease. But Cregger decided not to.

The movie is a reboot of the Resident Evil series. The old movies from 2002 made a billion dollars but weren't very faithful to the games. Cregger is trying something different. His movie is set in the game universe but doesn't adapt any specific game. Instead, it follows new characters and tells a new story. That made some hardcore fans nervous, but early reactions have been overwhelmingly positive.

The story follows Bryan (played by Austin Abrams), a medical courier who gets caught in a non-stop race for survival during one horrifying night. The cast also includes Zach Cherry, Kali Reis, and Paul Walter Hauser. Cregger co-wrote the script with Shay Hatten.

So if you see it in theaters, feel free to bolt as soon as the credits begin. No FOMO needed!
why_it_matters: It shows that not every movie has to follow the crowd — sometimes a director choosing to skip a popular trick is what makes a film special.

background_read: Resident Evil is a video game series that started in 1996, made by Capcom (a Japanese company that makes games). There are nine main games, plus many other side stories.
After-credits scenes became a tradition thanks to superhero movies, which often hide a short clip at the very end to set up the next film.
Movies based on games often get criticized by players when the story changes too much, so a new reboot (a fresh start for a series) makes fans both excited and nervous.
